newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MP says Islamists favour handing over power.
newsitem.headline: Turk MP says Islamists favour handing over power.

text.p: A senior Turkish conservative deputy said on Thursday the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP) favoured handing over the premiership soon to their True Path Party coalition allies to solve a government crisis.

"The RP looks favourably on handing over the prime minister's job. The handover will take place soon," a member of True Path's executive council who declined to be named told Reuters. He also said elections were to be held within a year.
"An election will be held within a year," the deputy said. Officials from the Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan were not immediately available for comment.
Ciller, the deputy prime minister, has asked Islamist Erbakan to make her prime minister in a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.
Their 11-month-old alliance has been losing deputies in a row with the secularist army over Islamist activism and is close to becoming a minority administration.
Turkish television said the parties had agreed on Ciller taking over the premiership in July and going to elections in October, but there was no independent confirmation.
